q01.title: Add more Flask bench cases, including quiet ones
q01.body:
Blot's accuracy is measured with real cases in [`bench/cases.json`](../blob/main/bench/cases.json). **Flask** (https://github.com/pallets/flask) already has 6 cases (4 warn, 2 quiet).

**What to add (2 cases):**
1. A **warning case** where the explaining commit is hidden behind a refactor or file move, like `0ec7f713` ("Split the App and Blueprint…") but on a different line. These are the cases plain `git blame` gets wrong.
2. A **quiet case**: an edit Blot should *not* warn about.

Tip: after `blot index` on a Flask clone, `blot why FILE:LINE` shows which commit explains a line and whether Blot traced past a refactor.

**How:**
- Copy an entry from `bench/cases.json` as a template. Each case needs `repo`, `at` (the commit to check out), `file`, `replace` (`["old text", "new text"]`, where the old text appears exactly once in the file), `expect` (`check`, `warn`: true/false, and for warn cases the `commit` the warning must cite) and a short `notes` line linking the PR or issue that explains the code.
- To try them quickly, put your new cases in a scratch file and run `blot bench --cases my-cases.json`; both must show `ok`. Then append them to the end of `bench/cases.json` (that's the file `blot bench` runs) and open the PR with only that file changed.
- Comment here before you start, so two people don't take the same issue.

See [`bench/README.md`](../blob/main/bench/README.md) for the fields and how to tell a real bug fix from a feature or refactor. No Python knowledge needed!

q01.body:
Hallo GiroCrab-Team,

ich würde gerne die **ADAC Kreditkarte (kontoführende Bank: Solaris SE)** als Konto in GiroCrab einbinden und frage an, ob dafür ein Konnektor geplant oder machbar ist.

### Ausgangslage

- Die ADAC Kreditkarten werden seit September 2024 von der Solaris SE bereitgestellt ([Bankpartnerseite des ADAC](https://www.adac.de/produkte/finanzdienstleistungen/kreditkarte/partner-solaris/)).
- Solaris betreibt **keinen FinTS-Server**, daher scheitert die generische FinTS-Anbindung (BLZ + URL) grundsätzlich.
- Eine PSD2-/Open-Banking-Einbindung ist für die ADAC Kreditkarte laut offizieller FAQ derzeit ebenfalls **nicht möglich**; ADAC kündigt dort eine Lösung "im Laufe des nächsten Jahres" an ([ADAC Kreditkarten FAQ](https://faq.adac-kreditkarte.de/hc/de/articles/21634644677149-Unterst%C3%BCtzt-Solaris-bzw-die-ADAC-Kreditkarte-derzeit-externe-Banking-Software-wie-Finanzblick-und-StarMoney)).
- Das frühere Freischalt-Portal `my.solarisbank.de` wurde mit der PSD2-Neuerung im März 2026 abgeschaltet.

### Machbarkeitsnachweise

- Banking4 ruft die ADAC-Kartenumsätze über einen Screen-Scraper ab ("ADAC Solaris Screen-Scraper", Subsembly-Modul `ScraperSessionAdacSolaris`; Änderungshistorie der Banking4-Updates).
- GiroCrab betreibt bereits Web-Portal-Konnektoren (z. B. Trade Republic, Hanseatic Bank) und mit Kontist einen Konnektor zu einer Solaris-Marke.
- Das ADAC-Kreditkartenbanking bietet einen CSV-Export der Umsätze als Fallback.

### Vorschlag

1. Mittelfristig: Web-Portal-Konnektor für das ADAC-Kreditkartenbanking, gern im Stil der bestehenden Portal-Konnektoren.
2. Sobald ADAC/Solaris die PSD2-Schnittstelle für die Karte freischaltet: Aufnahme in die Enable-Banking-/PSD2-Unterstützung.

Ich teste den Konnektor selbst gern aus, sobald eine Version verfügbar ist, und gebe dann Rückmeldung per Issue-Kommentar.

Vielen Dank für das tolle Projekt!

Use the existing fake transaction to cover a begin error and a commit error without a database. For the begin error, record whether the callback ran. q02.title: [Design System][CSS]: [data-theme='light'] CSS variables completely missing in tokens.css
q02.body:
### Problem Summary
In `src/styles/tokens.css`, `:root` is defined as Arounda dark theme (`--bg-canvas: #000000; --text-primary: #ffffff`), and `[data-theme='dark']` re-declares these dark values. Furthermore, line 197 includes a media query check `:root:not([data-theme='light'])`.

However, there is **no rule defining `[data-theme='light']` anywhere in the design tokens**.

### Location
- File: `src/styles/tokens.css` (lines 135–255)

### Impact
If a user, script, or browser preference sets `data-theme="light"` on the root `<html>` element:
- No light mode CSS variables exist to override `:root`.
- The background remains pitch black (`#000000`) and text remains white (`#ffffff`).
- Light mode is completely non-functional despite references to it in CSS media queries.

### Recommended Fix
1. Add a comprehensive `[data-theme='light']` token definition block in `tokens.css` providing light canvas backgrounds (`--bg-canvas: #ffffff; --bg-surface: #f9f9fb; --text-primary: #09090b;`, appropriate light border colors, and adjusted accent tints).
2. Ensure high color contrast ratios (WCAG AA / AAA) for all light mode text and surface combinations.
3. Add a unit test verifying both `[data-theme='dark']` and `[data-theme='light']` are fully defined in `tokens.css`.

q02.title: [BUG]: the Available cache ignores the environment, so one setting's list is shown for another
q02.body:
**Version**
vfox 1.1.0

**OS**
Linux (x86_64)

**Describe the bug**
`vfox search` caches the result of a plugin's `Available` hook in `<VFOX_HOME>/plugin/<name>/.available.cache` for `cache.availableHookDuration` (12 hours by default). The cache key is only the search arguments: in `internal/sdk/sdk.go`, `Available` uses `cacheKey := strings.Join(args, "##")`, or `empty` when there are none. The environment is not part of the key. A plugin whose hook reads an environment variable therefore gets the first result back for every value of that variable until the cache expires.

We found this while working on [version-fox/vfox-elixir#22](https://github.com/version-fox/vfox-elixir/issues/22). The plugin's `Available` hook returns the release list, or the hex.pm builds list when `VFOX_ELIXIR_MIRROR=hex` is set.

**To reproduce**
```
$ vfox search elixir                          # release list
Available versions:
 - 1.20-latest
 - 1.19-latest
 ...
$ VFOX_ELIXIR_MIRROR=hex vfox search elixir   # the same release list, from the cache
Available versions:
 - 1.20-latest
 ...
$ rm <VFOX_HOME>/plugin/elixir/.available.cache
$ VFOX_ELIXIR_MIRROR=hex vfox search elixir   # now the hook runs
Available versions:
 - main (pre-built from hex.pm)
 ...
```
Setting `cache.availableHookDuration` to `0s` also makes the second search call the hook.

**Expected**
A search under one environment should not show a result that the hook produced under another. Possible directions: include the values of the environment variables a hook reads in the cache key, let a plugin mark its `Available` result as not cacheable, or give a plugin a cache key of its own. q03.body:
A requirements file that names another index is treated as private from top to bottom: none of its packages is looked up. That is right for a company index. It is a dead end for the most common extra index there is, PyTorch's public one. Paste `jhj0517/Whisper-WebUI`, whose `requirements.txt` starts with `--extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128`:

> **No packages were checked**
> Not checked: requirements.txt names an index or source other than PyPI (an --index-url or --extra-index-url line, a [tool.uv] index or sources setting, a Pipfile source), so these may not be PyPI's packages and their names aren't sent to pypi.org: faster-whisper, gradio, gradio-i18n, matplotlib, pyannote.audio, pytubefix, ruamel.yaml, torch, and 2 more. To check them on that index, run uvx wheelgap --index-url with its URL in a checkout.

Two things are wrong for this visitor:

- Nothing here is private. `gradio` and `matplotlib` only exist on PyPI, and the other index is a public one that anyone can name. Projects that install PyTorch are among the ones with the most wheel trouble, and this line is how PyTorch's own instructions say to install it.
- The advice doesn't work. `--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128` makes wheelgap look every package up on that index alone, and it has no `gradio`.

- `_private()` and `_lookups()` in `site/check/driver.py`: `return source.kind != "pixi" and not source.pypi_only`.

- wheelgap sets `pypi_only` to false for any index option line. It doesn't say which line or which URL, so the driver has to read the option lines of the files it fetched itself.

**What to do**

- Keep a short list of public extra indexes in `driver.py`, starting with one host: `download.pytorch.org`. Adding a host is a reviewed change, with a comment saying who runs it.
- When a requirements file isn't PyPI-only, read its option l

### Problem Description

Older Hugging Face models ship sharded PyTorch weights with a `pytorch_model.bin.index.json` index. `analyze_model` routes every `*.index.json` to the SafeTensors parser, which then tries to read the `.bin` shards as SafeTensors files:

Passing one shard (`pytorch_model-00001-of-00002.bin`) only reports that shard.

- Like the SafeTensors path, passing a single shard next to its index should pick up the index.

### Additional Context

See `parse_safetensors_header` in `src/modelinfo/parsers/safetensors.py` for the existing index logic and `tests/test_binary_parsers.py` for how PyTorch archives are built in tests without installing torch.

# [Testing] Help validate ResQNet on real Android devices 📱

## Description

ResQNet is an experimental, open-source offline mesh messaging application built using Java and Android Nearby Connections.

Our automated tests and emulator tests cover important parts of the messaging and routing system, but we still need **real Android device testing** to validate how the application behaves over actual Bluetooth/Wi-Fi connections.

We're looking for Android developers and open-source contributors who can help us test the app on physical devices.

No code changes are required to get started!

## What needs testing?

### Basic testing — One Android device
- [ ] Install the maintainer-provided test APK.
- [ ] Launch the app successfully.
- [ ] Verify permissions and onboarding.
- [ ] Check basic UI navigation and diagnostics.
- [ ] Report crashes, unexpected behavior, or usability issues.

### Peer-to-peer testing — Two Android devices
- [ ] Discover a nearby device.
- [ ] Establish a connection.
- [ ] Exchange a test message.
- [ ] Disconnect and reconnect.
- [ ] Test with internet connectivity disabled while keeping the required local radios enabled.

### Multi-hop testing — Three Android devices
- [ ] Establish an A → B → C topology.
- [ ] Verify A and C cannot connect directly.
- [ ] Send a test SOS from A toward C.
- [ ] Confirm whether B relays the message.
- [ ] Record the hop count and delivery status.

q06.title: Research: UWB Precision Finding on Android
q06.body:
Split out of #251 ([analysis](https://github.com/parawanderer/OpenTagViewer/issues/251#issuecomment-6141798337)). This is research: nobody knows yet whether it can be done.

Goal: find out whether an Android phone with UWB hardware can range against an AirTag the way an iPhone's Precision Finding does (distance to about 10 cm, direction to within a few degrees).

What is known:

- Precision Finding uses Ultra Wideband (Apple's U1/U2 chip). The session is set up over Bluetooth first and keyed with the owner's keys. The protocol is Apple's own and there is no known public reverse engineering of it.
- Some Android phones have UWB hardware (Pixel 6 Pro and later Pro models, some Galaxy S Ultra, Plus and Fold models). Android exposes it through `androidx.core.uwb`, which follows the FiRa standard.

Steps:

1. Capture the Bluetooth traffic between an iPhone and its AirTag while Precision Finding runs (for example with an nRF52840 sniffer), and work out how the UWB session is negotiated.
2. Work out whether the session parameters the AirTag uses fall within what Android's FiRa API can configure.

Either step may be a dead end, and a write-up showing that it is one is a useful result. Relevant prior work and captures are welcome in this issue.

If this works out, the direction screen in the compass issue is where it would go.

> *Drafted by Claude Code*

q06.title: Transactional Outbox - [Feature]: Link consumer spans to the trace of the request
q06.body:
### Problem statement

The order service writes the W3C `traceparent` of the request into every event it publishes
(`traceParent` in the payload, filled by
[`CurrentTraceParent`](https://github.com/dmitriy-iliyov/spring-transactional-outbox/blob/main/order-service/src/main/java/io/github/outbox/order/tracing/CurrentTraceParent.java) in
[`OrderService`](https://github.com/dmitriy-iliyov/spring-transactional-outbox/blob/main/order-service/src/main/java/io/github/outbox/order/domain/OrderService.java)). The notification
service handles each consumed record in a span of its own trace (`spring.kafka.listener.observation-enabled`) and
uses the request's trace only for a log field,
`originTraceId` ([`ConsumerLogContext`](https://github.com/dmitriy-iliyov/spring-transactional-outbox/blob/main/notification-service/src/main/java/io/github/outbox/notification/consumer/ConsumerLogContext.java)).

In a tracing backend the two traces are unrelated: the request's trace ends at the HTTP response, and nothing leads
from it to the handling of its event or back. The trace id in the payload is enough to connect them with a span
link, which is how OpenTelemetry models messaging that runs after the producer has finished.

- **Difficulty:** Medium
- **Estimated time:** 1 day
- **Skills:** Java, Micrometer Tracing, OpenTelemetry, Spring Kafka, JUnit 5

q07.title: Run stdio servers in Docker containers
q07.body:
**Size:** medium to large

**Why:** a stdio MCP server runs with airlock's own user and filesystem. Running it in a container with no network and a read-only root is a much safer default for servers you didn't write.

**Behavior:** a server with `transport: stdio` and a `docker` block runs the command inside a container instead of directly:

```yaml
servers:
  - name: fetch
    transport: stdio
    docker:
      image: mcp/fetch:latest
      network: none
      read_only: true
      memory: 256m
    command: mcp-server-fetch
```

The container is started with `docker run -i --rm` and the same stdin and stdout piping the stdio backend uses, and removed when the backend closes.

**How:** start by building the `docker run` argument list from the config in a small pure function, so most of it is testable without Docker. Use the `docker` CLI rather than a Docker SDK dependency.

**Tests:** unit tests for the argument list (network, mounts, env, limits, quoting); a test behind the `integration` tag that runs a tiny image.

Comment with a plan before you start, especially on how env vars and secrets reach the container.

`PandasBinning` bins a complex source column (discarding the imaginary part with a `ComplexWarning`) instead of raising the reference's `Binning needs an integer or floating source column` `ValueError`.

## Reproduction

```python
import pandas as pd
from mloda.community.feature_groups.data_operations.row_preserving.binning.pandas_binning import PandasBinning
from mloda.testing.feature_groups.data_operations.helpers import calculate_with, make_feature_set

calculate_with(PandasBinning, pd.DataFrame({"x": [1 + 1j, 2 + 0j]}), make_feature_set("x__bin_2"))
# returns bins [0, 1]; expected ValueError
```

## Code pointers

- `mloda/community/feature_groups/data_operations/row_preserving/binning/pandas_binning.py` passes the shared `pandas_non_numeric_descriptor` (`row_preserving/arithmetic/pandas_numeric_source.py`), whose `is_numeric_dtype` counts complex as numeric. q08.title: [BUG]: the Available cache ignores the environment, so one setting's list is shown for another
q08.body:
**Version**
vfox 1.1.0

**OS**
Linux (x86_64)

**Describe the bug**
`vfox search` caches the result of a plugin's `Available` hook in `<VFOX_HOME>/plugin/<name>/.available.cache` for `cache.availableHookDuration` (12 hours by default). The cache key is only the search arguments: in `internal/sdk/sdk.go`, `Available` uses `cacheKey := strings.Join(args, "##")`, or `empty` when there are none. The environment is not part of the key. A plugin whose hook reads an environment variable therefore gets the first result back for every value of that variable until the cache expires.

We found this while working on [version-fox/vfox-elixir#22](https://github.com/version-fox/vfox-elixir/issues/22). The plugin's `Available` hook returns the release list, or the hex.pm builds list when `VFOX_ELIXIR_MIRROR=hex` is set.

**To reproduce**
```
$ vfox search elixir                          # release list
Available versions:
 - 1.20-latest
 - 1.19-latest
 ...
$ VFOX_ELIXIR_MIRROR=hex vfox search elixir   # the same release list, from the cache
Available versions:
 - 1.20-latest
 ...
$ rm <VFOX_HOME>/plugin/elixir/.available.cache
$ VFOX_ELIXIR_MIRROR=hex vfox search elixir   # now the hook runs
Available versions:
 - main (pre-built from hex.pm)
 ...
```
Setting `cache.availableHookDuration` to `0s` also makes the second search call the hook.

**Expected**
A search under one environment should not show a result that the hook produced under another. Possible directions: include the values of the environment variables a hook reads in the cache key, let a plugin mark its `Available` result as not cacheable, or give a plugin a cache key of its own. Errors returned by the hook are not cached today, which is correct.

q12.title: iOS SSH: close workspace swallows provider failures
q12.body:
The iOS SSH workspace close action can report completion while leaving the remote workspace alive when the provider close fails.

Current `origin/main` (`2eb9bee950ed7bafe590a88d946fefcb3f3e1e3f`): `Packages/iOS/CmuxMobileShell/Sources/CmuxMobileShell/MobileSSHComputers.swift:513-524` detaches local terminals, then calls `provider.closeWorkspace(id:)` through `try?`, discarding any error, and always refreshes the workspace list. A transient SSH disconnect, permission failure, or provider command error therefore produces no user-visible failure; the workspace remains on the server and can reappear on refresh. The row may disappear briefly only if the refresh is stale or unavailable.

A focused provider test can throw from `closeWorkspace`, assert that the runtime records a failure/notice and retains the workspace row, and verify that a successful close removes it. The fix belongs at this action boundary: preserve the error and surface it through the existing iOS SSH failure/terminal notice path instead of treating the mutation as successful.

This is S3 (`close` has a manual retry workaround) and difficulty 2 (one mobile action path plus provider failure coverage).

q13.body:
## Problem Overview
Centralized rating systems (like 5-star Uber reviews) are susceptible to platform manipulation, bias, and sudden account bans. Waymesh needs a decentralized Web-of-Trust where users cryptographically vouch for peers they have traveled with.

## Proposed Architecture & Solution
Implement Ed25519-signed vouchers in `waymesh-core`. After a successful Dual-OTP verified trip, Driver and Passenger can sign a `Vouch` attestment containing `{ vouch_target_id, trip_id, timestamp, score }`.

## Affected Crates & Files
- `crates/waymesh-core/src/crypto.rs`
- `crates/waymesh-core/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/waymesh-server/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/waymesh-server/src/db.rs`

## Step-by-Step Implementation Guide
1. Define `PeerVouch` struct with signature verification in `waymesh-core::crypto`.
2. Add database table `peer_vouches` storing valid signatures linking passenger and driver.
3. Compute an aggregated TrustScore based on verified vouch graph depth.
4. Add API endpoint `POST /api/v1/identities/:id/vouch` requiring valid Ed25519 signature.

## Definition of Done (Acceptance Criteria)
- [ ] Invalid signatures or forged vouchers are rejected with cryptographic error.
- [ ] Only parties with a completed `RideBooking` can submit mutual vouches for that trip.
- [ ] Unit tests verify tamper resistance.

q15.title: cli <tool> array flags do not accept a JSON array literal
q15.body:
## Problem

`codebase-memory-mcp cli <tool>` does not accept a JSON array literal for an array-typed argument. `--projects '["a","b"]'` becomes a one-element array containing the string `["a","b"]`.

Upstream accepts the literal (upstream PRs 2160 and 2227).

## Cause

`addTyped` (`src/cli/tool_args.zig:69-79`) appends the raw flag value as one string element for every `array` argument. It never tries to parse the value as JSON.

## Impact

Multi-value arguments only work by repeating the flag; the natural JSON form silently produces a wrong argument.

## Fix

When the value starts with `[`, parse it with yyjson and, if it is an array, append its elements; otherwise keep the current behavior. Simple change plus a CLI test.

## Evidence

Confirmed by reading `origin/main` (88f8d403).

q15.title: Explain "kept out of line" in health's log_status() comment
q15.body:
## What's wrong

Above `log_status()` in `apps/health/health.c`, the comment says:

> Kept out of line, so its buffer is on the stack only while a line is written, not through every major frame's FRAM write.

"Out of line" is compiler jargon. It's the opposite of *inline*: a separate function call, not merged into its caller. Most readers won't know the term, so the comment doesn't explain the `__noinline` on the function.

## Why `__noinline` is there

`step()` calls `boot_checkpoint()`, which writes FRAM. That's the deepest call chain in health's major frame: around 800 bytes of stack through the FRAM service and the SPI driver. Later, `step()` calls `log_status()`, which has a 160-byte `line` buffer.

`log_status()` is `static` and called from only one place, so an optimizing compiler would normally *inline* it: paste its body into `step()`. When it does, the buffer usually becomes part of `step()`'s stack frame for the whole of `step()`, including during the FRAM write. Health's deepest point would then be 160 bytes deeper, on a 2 KB stack (see `include/silversat/resource_map.h`, DS-44).

`__noinline` stops that. `log_status()` gets its own frame, which exists only while a line is being written, after the FRAM write has returned.

## What to do

Replace the sentence with plainer wording. Something like:

> Marked `__noinline`, so the compiler never merges it into step(). Its 160-byte buffer then uses stack only while a line is being written, instead of adding to step()'s stack during the FRAM write, which is health's deepest point.

Keep the rest of the comment.

## To learn from it

- Read about `inline` and stack frames: what does the compiler do with a function's local variables when it inlines the function?
- Try it. Remove `__noinline`, build for `nucleo_f446re`, and compare health's "least stack" in its status line on the board. Then put `__noinline` back.

Comment-only change, so this can go in its own PR or with the next change to `apps/health`.

q16.title: [BUG]: the Available cache ignores the environment, so one setting's list is shown for another
q16.body:
**Version**
vfox 1.1.0

**OS**
Linux (x86_64)

**Describe the bug**
`vfox search` caches the result of a plugin's `Available` hook in `<VFOX_HOME>/plugin/<name>/.available.cache` for `cache.availableHookDuration` (12 hours by default). The cache key is only the search arguments: in `internal/sdk/sdk.go`, `Available` uses `cacheKey := strings.Join(args, "##")`, or `empty` when there are none. The environment is not part of the key. A plugin whose hook reads an environment variable therefore gets the first result back for every value of that variable until the cache expires.

We found this while working on [version-fox/vfox-elixir#22](https://github.com/version-fox/vfox-elixir/issues/22). The plugin's `Available` hook returns the release list, or the hex.pm builds list when `VFOX_ELIXIR_MIRROR=hex` is set.

**To reproduce**
```
$ vfox search elixir                          # release list
Available versions:
 - 1.20-latest
 - 1.19-latest
 ...
$ VFOX_ELIXIR_MIRROR=hex vfox search elixir   # the same release list, from the cache
Available versions:
 - 1.20-latest
 ...
$ rm <VFOX_HOME>/plugin/elixir/.available.cache
$ VFOX_ELIXIR_MIRROR=hex vfox search elixir   # now the hook runs
Available versions:
 - main (pre-built from hex.pm)
 ...
```
Setting `cache.availableHookDuration` to `0s` also makes the second search call the hook.

**Expected**
A search under one environment should not show a result that the hook produced under another. Possible directions: include the values of the environment variables a hook reads in the cache key, let a plugin mark its `Available` result as not cacheable, or give a plugin a cache key of its own. Errors returned by the hook are not cached today, which is correct.

q17.title: GraphQL `getPriceHistory` reads both networks at once
q17.body:
### Background

The REST history route filters by network (`src/api/rest.ts` line 332: `WHERE pair_key = $1 AND window = $2 AND network = $3`).

The GraphQL resolver for the same data does not. In `src/api/graphql.ts` (lines 675 to 701) the conditions are only:

```ts
const conditions: string[] = ['pair_key = $1', 'window = $2']
```

`price_aggregates` holds testnet and mainnet rows. On an instance that ingests both, `getPriceHistory` returns the buckets of both chains mixed in one list, with nothing in a bucket to tell them apart. A chart built on it is wrong in a way that looks only noisy.

The same resolver has more loose ends:

- The pair key is built from the raw arguments (line 675), so `xlm`/`usdc` or `native` returns an empty list with no error.
- `limit` goes through `Math.min(limit, 1000)` (line 689). A negative number reaches Postgres and comes back as a masked internal error.
- An unknown `window` (for example `"2h"`) is not rejected. It falls back to 60 seconds for the size check (line 661) and then matches no rows.
- The field has no `network` argument, although `oracle`, `volumes` and `spreads` in the same schema do.

### What to build

- Filter by network. Add an optional `network` argument (`testnet` or `mainnet`, default the active network) and reject any other value with `INVALID_INPUT`, as `oracle` does at line 763.
- Resolve the pair like `getPrice` does and raise `PAIR_NOT_FOUND` for an unknown one.
- Reject an unknown `window` and a `limit` below 1 with `INVALID_INPUT`; clamp a large `limit`.
- Do not change the bucket fields.
- Regenerate the generated files, because the schema changes.

- `src/api/graphql.ts` lines 380 to 394 (schema) and 622 to 715 (resolver)
- `src/__tests__/graphqlPriceHistory.test.ts`

### What to do

- cross-fitted target encoding — sklearn's `TargetEncoder` (1.3+) does cross-fit, so

The pinned ansible-lockdown roles apply Level 1 **and** Level 2 rules by default: their `*_level_1` / `*_level_2` variables only steer the audit output, not remediation. So the hardened images are stricter than "CIS Level 1" suggests, and the docs deliberately avoid calling them Level 1.

**Options**
- Restrict remediation to Level 1 (tag filtering in `ansible/linux.yml`, or per-rule overrides in `ansible/vars/cis_*.yml`). Needs verification against each pinned role version.
- Or keep Level 1 + 2 and document it everywhere.

Whichever you pick, add or update a test (see `tests/unit/test_ansible_files.py`) and measure the result with the role's own audit, which has not been run yet.

q20.title: Run the kind platform end to end on macOS (Apple Silicon, Intel) and Linux arm64
q20.body:
From the [roadmap](https://github.com/joezuchora/golden-path-k8s/blob/main/ROADMAP.md) (*help wanted*, source D-056).

**Goal:** run the kind platform end to end on a platform it hasn't been run on yet, and report the result.

Today Windows (Docker Desktop) and Linux amd64 (GitHub's Ubuntu runner, on every PR) run `make kind-up` and every suite end to end. For macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Linux arm64, `tools/install.sh` and `tools/checksums.lock` cover the platform, but the lock entries come from published checksums (`--lock-platform`). Per D-056, the first real install on a platform is what proves the file.

**Steps**
```
make doctor            # local profile; see docs/getting-started.md
make tools             # pinned, checksum-verified CLIs into ./.bin
make kind-up
make e2e-all
make kind-down
```

**Done when:** a comment or PR reports the OS, architecture, container engine and its memory setting, the `make doctor` output, and the suite results. Fixes for any platform-specific failure come as a PR with a D-entry (and an F-entry for any external fact, from its primary source), plus a row in [known issues](https://github.com/joezuchora/golden-path-k8s/blob/main/docs/known-issues.md) where it fits.

One platform per report is fine; say which one you're taking.

q20.title: Spike: KCL (function-kcl) instead of go-templating for a composition
q20.body:
From the [roadmap](https://github.com/joezuchora/golden-path-k8s/blob/main/ROADMAP.md) (*help wanted: a spike*, source D-044, [ADR-0011](https://github.com/joezuchora/golden-path-k8s/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-composition-function-go-templating.md)).

**Context:** every composition (`azure` and `local`) uses `function-go-templating` + `function-auto-ready`. That keeps one Helm-style templating language for platform engineers and reviewers. ADR-0011 records `function-kcl` as the stronger option *if composition logic grows typed or complex*. A composition that outgrows templates can use function-kcl in its own pipeline without changing the XRD API.

**Spike:** port one existing composition (for example the `local` PostgreSQLInstance) to `function-kcl` in its own pipeline, and compare it with the go-templating version on:
- readability for a reviewer who knows Helm but not KCL
- how errors surface in `crossplane composition render` (offline, as `make validate` runs it)
- reading the XR's Namespace for derived tags (ADR-0007), which go-templating does via `ExtraResources`
- pinning, digest and release cadence of the function package

**Done when:** a PR adds the spike composition with a render golden file that passes `make validate`, plus a short write-up recommending keep, adopt per composition, or switch. A recommendation to change the default needs a D-entry revisiting D-044 and an ADR-0011 update. F-entries for external facts must come from primary sources.

q20.title: Replace GH CLI w/ `peter-evans/create-pull-request` in `reusable-pip-compile` for commit signing
q20.body:
https://github.com/peter-evans/create-pull-request has `sign-commits: true` with native logic for producing signatures by interacting with GitHub API and recreating the commit objects/tree in a loop. It's not something I'd recommend reimplementing and maintaining.

I've tested it in a few places. Here's one: https://github.com/ansible/awx-plugins/pull/205 / https://github.com/ansible/awx-plugins/pull/206 / https://github.com/ansible/awx-plugins/pull/207.

It uses the GHA bot (`github-actions[bot]`) but will work with a GH App installation token too.

One kinda thing that caught me by surprise was that my jobs started timing out because I was keeping it tight before signing, and then I realized that this mechanism has built-in delays proportional to the number of commits needing signing because it needs to hit API for each and the action is trying not to get rate-limited. Because my PR includes a lot of individual commits, I needed to raise said timeout. It was instant with an unsigned `git push`.

Here's a bump PR example: https://github.com/ansible/awx-plugins/pull/215.
